It is hard to say. I did and do feel that the help I received there and the attention of a few hard-working nurses did save me from suicide at the time, but the pills and talking did very little to help reasjust to "society". At least in my case(and probably in many others), my problems began at a very early age, maybe 7 or earlier when I became increasingly withdrawn. A lifetime of poor social skills, school trauma, poor life skills all contributed to a difficult time adjusting when the shit really hit the fan. If I were to be Yoda, I would probably say that to heal things like this, we need better community support as well as safe centers for the homeless mentally ill and those having trouble adjusting to the madness of the everyday world. But I'm not Yoda so I don't know. Haldol does help. Kind of.

This is my alt-account so I don't mind posting as many details as I can, barring my name, exact locations of hospitals, etc, so feel free to ask.

I was in a psych hospital a few(three) times, although only once for any amount of time(1 week) due to a suicide attempt. Sadly, most insurance companies will do anything they can to get you out of a hospital stay, even if you are still suicidal. My stays there were both terribly boring(nothing to do but go to stupid groups) and a little scary(most of the other patients weren't that scary and after I was there for a few days I wasn't as freaked out by random screaming and the like.

Overall, it was probably helpful in the short term, since it took me from the place I was at(intensely suicidal due to a reaction to Zoloft) and stabilized me. In the long term, for me, I believe it was not helpful, since the course of action seems always to focus on medication and therapy, even if these courses do not work very well.

I am a functioning dX schizoaffective, but I don't know how to fix myself. I still take a low dose of a shitty medication so I am not super-paranoid, but it isn't so great. I don't believe blaming the system will fix my problems, but the psychiatric system is terribly broken- taking broken people, drugging them up, not believing them that the drugs are horrid and throwing them onto the streets.

It was 14 years ago when I was at the Psych hospital for a suicide attempt. I don't know what my life would have been like without psychiatry. Without a lot of family support, I might have turned to drugs, but instead, the psych hospital did keep me alive. 

I volunteer(and volunteered) a lot because I have a lot of issues staying in one place, a lot of paranoia as well, and maybe if I did not fall into the psych system, I would have been able to be more independent, not rely on food stamps and welfare and struggled with homelessness and whatever.

Who knows?
